note: The contract between three repos that all report into one PostHog project. Event names and property names are exact: a property spelled levelId here is levelId everywhere, and a site that emits level_id silently drops out of every cross-property query. Copy this file into the other repos rather than retyping it, and change it here first.

site.note: Added by the track() wrapper, never by a call site.

contentVersion.note: A stamp identifying the vocab and level data the session ran against. sessions.json, vocab.json and syllables.json carry NO version marker today - adding one is part of G1. Without it, a vocab swap or a level reorganisation silently merges incomparable data into one series. With it, every query can segment on content, and 'before and after we changed the words' is a filter rather than a guess.

designNote.structureOverIdentity: Prefer properties that describe WHAT HAPPENED over properties that name WHICH ITEM it happened to. syllableCount, expectedTones, wrongIndexes and speaker all survive a complete vocabulary replacement, because they describe the shape of the task rather than its content. word and levelId do not. The highest-value output in the plan - the tone confusion matrix - is built entirely from expectedTones against chosenTones, so it accumulates across any number of vocab swaps without a break.
designNote.levelIdIsALabel: levelId is a human-readable display string like 'Level 1: Animals (Ẹranko) — speaker2'. It embeds the level number, the theme and the speaker, so reorganising levels can reuse a levelId for different words. That is worse than a rename: a rename ends one series and starts another, while a reuse merges two series that should not be compared. Treat levelId as a label for reading reports, never as the key an analysis depends on. Group by category, syllableCount, speaker and contentVersion instead.
designNote.adsOffOnGamePages: The constraint below says the Google Ads tag must not load on the game pages, but until 2026-09 it did: track.js init() called loadAds() unconditionally, and game-events.js calls init(). Verified in production - gtag/js?id=AW-... was requested on /phonics/, /tones/ and /vocab/. The fix is init's `ads` option, which game-events.js sets to false while page-events.js leaves true, so the tag loads on the landing page and the marketing site and nowhere a child plays. Do not remove that flag without re-reading childDirectedConstraint.

$pageview.hook: yorubadict: handleRoute (app.js:651) or capture_pageview:'history_change'. games landing + speaknigeria: page-events.js. games phonics/tones: game-events.js.
$pageview.note: The dictionary is an SPA; the default one-per-load reports a single view for a visit that read twenty entries. See ANALYTICS.md §6.1.

consent_granted.hook: consent.js, on an affirmative answer to the notice
consent_granted.note: The record Google's EU user consent policy requires: which notice text was shown, and when it was agreed to. Only fired for a yes - a refusal leaves nothing to retain. noticeVersion maps to the wording in consent.js; never reuse a version for different text.

spelling_page_view.note: The word-ad landing page. 829 ambiguous spellings are self-canonical and in the sitemap.

sense_chosen.note: The word-ad conversion: landed on a toneless spelling, saw it was several words, picked one.

search_settled.hook: end of a search episode - query unchanged ~1.5s, or blur/clear/navigation. NOT per keystroke: onSearchInput debounces at 60ms (app.js:766).

refinedFromPrevious.note: True when this query is a prefix extension or diacritic variant of the previous episode - i.e. the reader was still typing.

search_none_matched.hook: the 'none of these' control on the result list
search_none_matched.note: Only build the control if someone will read the queue. See ANALYTICS.md §6.4.

building_block_followed.hook: [data-search-form] branch of the entryContent delegated handler
building_block_followed.note: The project's thesis, and a primary conversion.

hedge_explainer_opened.note: A reader weighing a claim we already flagged as uncertain. The place to ask a question later, per §6.4.

outbound_click.hook: yorubadict: interceptLinks. games landing + speaknigeria: page-events.js delegated click.

outbound_form_click.hook: page-events.js delegated click; the three Google Form links in speaknigeria.org/courses.html
outbound_form_click.note: A click, not a submission. Google Forms cannot redirect to a confirmation URL.

game_start.hook: loadLevel on the first level of a playlist (phonics:407, tones:719)
game_start.note: Secondary conversion only - it fires on nearly every non-bounce ad click. See §7.1.

game_opened.hook: page-events.js delegated click, games landing page only
game_opened.note: Clicking from the games landing page into a game. The gap between this and game_start is people who opened a game and never picked a playlist - the drop-off an ad pays for and does not get. Requires the game's path prefix in page-events.js: a game missing from that regex silently reports no conversion.

word.note: The vocab key, e.g. aja_dog. Stable while the word exists; absent after a vocab swap. Never the only thing an analysis groups by.

tonePattern.note: The word's tone shape as a dash-joined string, e.g. mid-high-low. Survives a complete vocab replacement, so 'which tone shapes are hard' stays answerable across content changes where 'which words are hard' does not.

answer_checked.hook: tones: checkAnswer (tones:915), both branches already exist. phonics: checkWinCondition (phonics:564) is a bare if with NO else - the wrong-answer path must be added. vocab: handleChoice, both branches.
answer_checked.note: The highest-value event in the plan. expectedTones against chosenTones gives a confusion matrix of Yoruba tone perception. Do NOT introduce scoring - see the comment above playWrong in tones/app.js.

chosenWord.note: vocab only - the word actually picked, so a wrong pick names the confusion

choiceCount.note: vocab only - how many words were offered, since a level too small to fill four changes the odds

audio_replayed.hook: full word: playFullWordAudio (phonics:471, tones:794). syllable: handleSyllableClick (phonics:531), playRecordedSyllable (tones:879).
audio_replayed.note: Doubles as a data-quality signal: a syllable replayed far more than its neighbours is probably an unclear recording, actionable back in yoruba-student-dict.

level_complete.hook: loadLevel advancing past the last word
level_complete.note: PRIMARY conversion, and the safest one: it maps onto the 'quizzes completed' example in the Ad Grants policy. sessions.json levels run 3-12 words, median 8, so it is reachable in one sitting.

level_abandoned.hook: pagehide ONLY - never visibilitychange. These are played in classrooms, where a teacher switching tabs is normal and is not abandonment.

share_link_created.hook: the share control - requires URL routing, which neither game has today
share_link_created.note: PRIMARY conversion. A share click is observable; whether anyone opened it is not (the Web Share API gives no success callback on mobile).

conversions.note: Google Ads conversion actions, per ANALYTICS.md §7.3. A conversion must discriminate between a good click and a bad one. Count: One, never Every.
conversions.childDirectedConstraint: games.speaknigeria.org is played by children (Speak Nigeria's courses are ages 5-17), which brings COPPA into scope. COPPA treats cookies as personal information on a child-directed site, and its narrow 'support for internal operations' exception covers basic analytics but NOT advertising. So the Google Ads tag must NOT load on /phonics/ or /tones/. The resolution: advertise the games LANDING page, which is what an adult searching Google actually reaches, put the Ads tag only there, and make game_opened the conversion. It discriminates well - not everyone who lands opens a game - and it fires on the adult-facing page. level_complete and share_link_created stay as PostHog events for curriculum insight, but can no longer be Google Ads conversions.
conversions.childAudienceNote: The games are played by children in Speak Nigeria's classes (ages 5-17), so /phonics/ and /tones/ are a mixed audience: a child may be the direct user, though the sites are marketed to parents and teachers and no advertising is displayed anywhere. That is not the same as child-directed, and it does not bar the Ads tag or conversion tracking. Two choices follow from it anyway, both cheap: ad_personalization stays denied everywhere (Ad Grants cannot use it regardless), and session replay stays off on the game pages - a judgement about recording children's screens, not a legal requirement. answer_checked already carries what replay was wanted for.
